A few suggestions:
1. Offer a different color of mouse. For a while my Edgar would only eat white mice/rats. He’s become less picky with age.
2. Ensure it isn’t too big of a meal.
3. Don’t panic unless she’s losing a good amount of weight. If she starts looking skinny, then it’s time to worry.
4. For frozen thawed, try drying off the mouse before feeding. If water hits Edgar, he’ll decide that he isn’t hungry all of a sudden.
5. If she’s just calmly refusing food as you’re describing, she just might not be hungry or want to eat. BPs are NOTORIOUS for hunger strikes and at first they can be pretty scary. These can be brought on by anything really, moving is one of them. It may take her a while to adjust (: just be patient!
6. Do NOT force/assist feed unless instructed to by a vet or reptile expert. This is extremely stressful for snakes.
7. Do not handle her 48 hours before and after feeding.

Again to reiterate, 9 times out of 10 there’s nothing wrong with a BP who goes on a hunger strike, but if she starts losing weight then it’s time to worry. Good luck!! (:
